contributions.improvement: Comprehensive feature extraction in spatial and frequency domains
contributions.implementation_detail: Proposes the Spatial-Frequency Enhanced Mamba Block (SFMB) to enhance Mamba in both spatial and frequency domains.

experiment_setup.training_details: Experiments are conducted with the PyTorch toolbox and a single NVIDIA GeForce A100 GPU. Training samples are resized to 128x128. No data augmentation beyond resizing is applied. The number of training epochs is set to 30. The batch size is set to 20. AdamW optimizer [58] is adopted with the learning rate set to 10^-3 and the weight decay set to 10^-2. The model is warmed up for 800 iterations with a linearly growing learning rate from 10^-5 to 10^-3. The exponential learning rate decay is used during the training. For hyper-parameters, the number of SFMGs for three branches is 3. The number of SFMBs in each SFMG is 2. The loss hyper-parameters a1, a2, a3 and a4 are set to 0.5, 0.5, 1 and 1, respectively.

title: SDCM: Simulated Densifying and Compensatory Modeling Fusion for Radar-Vision 3-D Object Detection in Internet of Vehicles

contributions.improvement: Achieve dense 4-D radar point clouds
contributions.implementation_detail: SimDen module designed to generate dense radar point clouds through Gaussian simulation of key points (from 3-D KDE) and outline generation based on curvature simulation.
contributions.improve_from: Sparse 4-D radar point clouds leading to poor 3-D representation

contributions.improvement: Reduce the affects of vision data representation degradation
contributions.implementation_detail: RCM module designed to compensate for deficiencies caused by visual features' degradation through radar features compensation under several sizes of receptive field.
contributions.improve_from: Vision data exhibiting representation degradation under low-light, long distance detection, and dense occlusion scenes

contributions.improvement: Reduce heterogeneity and achieve feature interaction fusion
contributions.implementation_detail: MMIF module designed to extract and model effective information from feature tensor difference values using Mamba mechanism for long-range dependencies capture and linear complexity.
contributions.improve_from: Heterogeneity between radar and vision data

contributions.improvement: Achieve best performance with lower parameter quantity and faster inference speed
contributions.implementation_detail: The overall SDCM framework avoids high computational complexity mechanisms like Transformer and Cross-Attention for feature extraction and multi-modality fusion.

limitations: No obvious advantages on the detection of Cyclist category, as SimDen module focuses more on point cloud densifying of persons on bicycles/motorcycles instead of the entirety, leading to false detection.

SimDen module brings -1.84 improvements in EAA mAP because depth filtering depends on the mode value of point clouds depth, and background influences depth value distribution when instances are out of the driving corridor.

datasets.details: A new autonomous driving dataset containing 64-layer LIDAR, 3+1-D radar, and stereo camera data, mainly from Delft. Uses five-scan point cloud data to detect Car, Pedestrian, and Cyclist categories. Evaluated using 3-D mAP in Entire Annotated Area (EAA) and Driving Corridor (DC).

A novel autonomous driving dataset from Singapore and Suzhou, China. Contains 3+1-D radar point clouds in continuous sequences with 3-D annotations and multimodal complete information from 64-layers LIDAR, camera, and GNSS. Scenes include daylight, night, and exposure. Evaluated using 3-D mAP and BEV mAP for Car, Pedestrian, Cyclist, and Truck.

A small autonomous driving dataset containing 64-layers LIDAR, 3+1-D radar, and stereo camera data captured in Germany urban and outskirt roads. Contains three object categories: Car, Pedestrian, and Cyclist, with detailed 3-D bounding box annotations. Evaluated using 3-D mAP and BEV mAP in three difficulty levels (Easy, Moderate, Hard).

experiment_setup.training_details: Training and testing split ratios are 4:1 for VoD and Astyx HiRes 2019, and 5:1 for TJ4DRadSet. All training was conducted on eight NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs within OpenPCDet Platform, using Python 3.8, PyTorch 2.0.0, CUDA 11.8, and Ubuntu 20.04. Inference uses Half-Precision Floating-Point (FP16). Training parameters (epochs, batch size, optimizer type, initial learning rate, decay strategy, and LR decay) are detailed in Table II. For SimDen, YOLOv8-Seg large model is used for instance segmentation, Gauss kernel and Silverman bandwidth rule for 3-D KDE, top 4 high density values for Gaussian simulation, 20 edge points for curvature estimation, and 200 simulated points per instance. For RCM and MMIF, input feature maps are 320x320, with 2 convolution layers and 3 different receptive fields. MMIF channel transformation uses Reshape operator (80x80, 128 to 128x16 channels), with 2 DWConv2D-SiLU layers for feature enhancement. RadarPillarNet and VMamba are used as backbones for radar and vision data, respectively. Faster-RCNN-like Region Proposal Network (RPN) is adopted as the detection head.

contributions.improvement: Synergistic modeling of global context and local details

contributions.improve_from: Existing Mamba-based methods (which often lead to local feature attenuation) and conventional Visual State Space (VSS) modules.

Comprehensive data augmentation strategy tailored for medical imaging including: (1) Spatial Transformations (rotational augmentation, elastic deformations), (2) Intensity Perturbations (window width/level shifts, local brightness modulation, Gaussian noise), (3) Anatomical Integrity Preservation (Third-order spline interpolation).

contributions.improvement: Enhanced perception of fine-grained structures and global semantic consistency, strengthened segmentation capability for small-scale lesions.
contributions.implementation_detail: Designed a cross-color-modality fusion framework (CFCM Net) that uses mirrored reinforcement of BCF (Bimodal Cross-stream Fusion) to align semantic information with spatial structures, enabling dynamic fusion and collaborative modeling of diverse feature information and color space data.
contributions.improve_from: Existing methods that struggle with feature entanglement and ambiguous inter-class distributions when handling small-scale lesions and blurred boundaries.

contributions.improvement: Enhanced expression of low-frequency structures in deep features, suppressed high-frequency noise interference, and improved modeling accuracy and anti-aliasing capability for abstract semantic information.
contributions.implementation_detail: Proposed LFFP (Low Frequency Focusing Perception Block) which integrates Gaussian filtering with channel attention mechanisms.
contributions.improve_from: Transformer architectures' high-dimensional feature channels at low-resolution stages are prone to semantic entanglement and amplification of high-frequency noise.

contributions.improvement: Enhanced ability to represent heterogeneous features in the color dimension, strengthened perception of hidden lesions and similar textures.

contributions.improve_from: Conventional feature extraction pathways confined to modeling within a single-color space, exhibiting insufficient capacity to capture color characteristics.

limitations: The increase in model complexity is mainly due to the repeated integration of ViT modules during the encoding phase, leading to larger parameters and FLOPs.

The current model entails a considerable number of parameters.

experiment_setup.training_details: The proposed framework was trained in two stages. Stage 1: A baseline neural network was trained for 50 epochs with a batch size of 8. title: Analytical and experimental investigation of vibration response for the cracked fluid-filled thin cylindrical shell under transport condition

proposed_method_detail.method_name: Free Vibration Response Solution Method for Cracked Fluid-Filled Thin Cylindrical Shells (FTCS-SC) and Natural Frequency Isoline-Based State Recognition Method

limitations: Computational resource limitations (processing time, storage capacity, memory requirements) necessitated the use of six separate modeling domains instead of a single statewide domain.
Emission inventories are subject to uncertainties regarding the locations and release rates of emission sources.

Air quality modeling (CALPUFF) inherently involves numerous approximations, leading to uncertainties in how emission sources are represented and in the meteorological fields, which can cause inaccuracies in DPM concentration estimations.
Calculation of cancer risk based on DPM concentrations involves numerous parameters that influence DPM uptake, and the OEHHA guidance used tends to be overly conservative, introducing uncertainty.

Sources of uncertainty in risk estimates include extrapolating toxicity data from animals to humans, uncertainty in estimating emissions, uncertainty in air dispersion models, and uncertainty in exposure estimates.

The study is based on 2012 and 2017 emissions data, which may differ significantly from current levels, leading to a disconnect between the model assessment year and the present day. Future studies will need to focus on more recent estimates.
Extrapolations from 2012 to 2017 results are not recommended as new emission reduction plans implemented since 2017 are not being accounted for.

title: Gradual machine learning for medical image classification via evolutionary feature fusion

contributions.improvement: Develop a novel gradual machine learning paradigm based on evolutionary multi-view feature fusion for medical image classification.
contributions.implementation_detail: Utilizes evolutionary Feature Selection (FS) to effectively fuse multi-view features and construct high-quality factors for test images to improve inference performance of Gradual Machine Learning (GML), facilitating Medical Image Classification (MIC) scenarios with scarce labeled data.
contributions.improve_from: Existing MIC methods that rely on a single Deep Learning (DL) backbone, resulting in limited robustness and sensitivity to data distribution.

contributions.improvement: Propose a novel co-evolutionary mechanism to optimize feature selection, enabling effective multi-view feature fusion.
contributions.implementation_detail: Proposes a novel Multi-Population Evolutionary Algorithm (MPEA) to perform FS process, incorporating a multi-population generation strategy, an environment selection strategy, and dynamically adjusted evolution operators. The MPEA effectively filters out irrelevant features while achieving deep fusion of feature vectors, thereby generating high-quality feature factors for test images used in GML.
contributions.improve_from: Existing FS methods that do not adequately consider the complementarity between features and the overall performance of feature combinations.

contributions.improvement: Achieve superior and more stable classification performance compared to existing methods across diverse medical datasets.
contributions.implementation_detail: Extensive experiments conducted on eight medical datasets demonstrate that our method (GML-FS) achieves higher and more stable classification performance compared to the existing State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) methods.

experiment_setup.training_details: For DL models: Input medical images are resized to 224x224 pixels and normalized using the mean and standard deviation (std) values calculated from the respective training sets. Horizontal flipping is applied to images with a certain probability. All neural network architectures are trained using the Adam optimizer with an initial learning rate of 0.001. The exponential decay rate for the first moment estimates is 0.9, while for the second moment estimates is 0.999. Each architecture is trained for 50 epochs. For Evolutionary FS methods: The population size N is 100, the maximum number of objective function evaluations is set to 10000, and the KNN classifier uses K=7. Other major parameter settings follow the recommended values from their original papers. For the proposed MPEA, the population size (N) is 100, the maximum generation number (Imax) is 20, the size of the external archive (E1) is 10, and the neighborhood size (T) is 7.

datasets.details: Collected by a team from Huazhong University of Science and Technology at Shanghai Changhai Hospital, consisting of microscopic hyperspectral images of common bile duct tissue slices stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E), with a slice thickness of 10 µm. Contains 349 high-quality scenes (HSIs) with segmentation labels for training and testing (880 microscopic hyperspectral scenes from 174 individuals). 689 scenes contain partial cancerous regions, 49 scenes are entirely cancerous, and 142 scenes do not contain any cancerous regions. Cancerous areas were precisely annotated by experienced pathologists. Input spectral range 550 nm to 775 nm (30 spectral channels). Total 60 spectral bands covering 550-1000 nm. Spatial resolution 1024 x 1280 pixels.

experiment_setup.training_details: The HMFF-ST model was implemented using the PyTorch framework and executed on an RTX 4070 Ti GPU (12 GB). Adaptive Moment Estimation (Adam) optimizer with an initial learning rate set to 4 × 10-4. The learning rate is halved every 50 epochs and further adjusted by a cosine annealing scheduler. The training batch size is set to 2, and the total number of training iterations is 300. The dataset was randomly split into training and testing sets at an 8:2 ratio (280 images for training, 69 images for testing). Data augmentation included randomly cropping 5000 smaller patches of size 256 x 256 x 30. Half of the images were randomly cropped and rotated (0 to 3 times by 90 degrees), then flipped horizontally and vertically. The other half involved randomly cropping four 128 × 128 × 30 patches from four different images and placing them in the four corners of a new 256 x 256 x 30 composite image.

experiment_setup.training_details: The network architectures in Fig. 2 are implemented with pytorch. The generator encoder comprises two down-sampling layers with a stride size of 2, and three decoders consist of two up-sampling convolution layers with a stride size of 1. The CBFNet comprises four AdaLIN residual blocks [36] in the transformation branch and four residual blocks in the reconstruction branch. We use the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.0002, betal of 0.5, and beta2 of 0.999 to train the generator and the discriminator. For data augmentation, we flipped the images horizontally with a probability of 0.5, resized them to 286 × 286, and randomly cropped them to 256 x 256. All experiments are done on a workstation with an Ubuntu 18.04.2 LTS system equipped with NVIDIA TITAN RTX GPU. The model's parameters are 105M and occupy approximately 11 g of memory. During the training phase, we only use image-level labels (class labels) for weakly supervised image segmentation. title: Expression guided medical condition detection via the Multi-Medical Condition Image Dataset

proposed_method_detail.method_name: Bi-stream framework with Adaptive Weight Fusion (AWF)

contributions.improvement: improved classification accuracy and better performance in recognizing acute medical conditions
contributions.implementation_detail: A Bi-stream network structure is proposed to effectively leverage both postural features from the overall image and facial expression features from the extracted facial images.
contributions.improve_from: methods relying on only one source of information (e.g., only posture or only facial expression)

contributions.improvement: more robust to ambiguity and noise interference, reduced likelihood of errors in classification
contributions.implementation_detail: An Adaptive Weight Fusion (AWF) mechanism is introduced, which dynamically adjusts the fusion weight to emphasize the relatively complete feature components while suppressing the weaker ones.
contributions.improve_from: existing feature fusion methods (e.g., simple concatenation or addition)

limitations: Relying only on image modalities such as facial images and whole images may not allow for further breakthroughs in detection accuracy metrics.
Challenges when dealing with samples that exhibit subtle or ambiguous facial expressions, where the signals for category features are insufficient.
Distinguishing between similar postures presents complexity, as the model may struggle to accurately classify samples that share similar postures but belong to different categories.

datasets.details: A novel benchmark dataset designed to encompass a broader range of abnormalities, namely Heart Infarction, Headache, Fall, and Normal. It contains a total of 4,000 raw images. The dataset is split into 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% test sets. Images are sourced from stock photography, Shutterstock, iStock, E-FPDS dataset, and NTU RGB+D 120 dataset.

experiment_setup.training_details: The entire framework is built on the Tensorflow toolbox with Keras library. Training is performed on an Nvidia Quadro RTX 8000 GPU, with a batch size of 64 and 100 epochs. All images are resized to 224 x 224 before training. The Adam optimizer is used. An early stopping mechanism is set to avoid over-fitting, terminating training if validation accuracy does not show significant improvement for 10 consecutive epochs. The initial learning rate is 1e-3, dynamically reduced by a factor of 0.5.

title: FATFusion: A functional–anatomical transformer for medical image fusion

contributions.improvement: Better preservation of modality-specific intrinsic characteristics
contributions.implementation_detail: Designed a functional multiscale branch (FMB) and an anatomical multiscale branch (AMB) to extract interscale characteristics belonging to each modality separately.
contributions.improve_from: Existing MIF algorithms that concatenate modalities or use parallel branches without considering distinct characteristics.

contributions.improvement: Enhanced global complementary information interaction
contributions.implementation_detail: Elaborated functional-guided transformer modules (FGTMs) and anatomical-guided transformer modules (AGTMs) to communicate and gather perceived features for global complementary information interaction.
contributions.improve_from: ConvNet-based methods with limited receptive fields.

contributions.improvement: Unsupervised end-to-end training
contributions.implementation_detail: Designed pixel loss and total variation loss to guide the deep fusion model to leverage significant properties without requiring ground truth.

limitations: The model relies on pre-registered paired images, and obtaining fully registered medical data directly in clinical scenarios poses considerable challenges.

datasets.details: 354 source image pairs (SPECT-MRI) split into training (319), testing (20), and validation (15). Images were cropped into 120x120 patches for training. Also used 10 PET-MRI pairs for generalization testing.

experiment_setup.training_details: Unsupervised training using Adam Optimizer for 10 epochs with a learning rate of 0.03 and batch size of 8. Data augmentation via overlap cropping into 120x120 patches with a crop size of 20. Loss function includes pixel loss and total variation loss with trade-off parameters λ1=0.03, λ2=1000, λ3=10, and λ4=100.

title: FCSU-Net: A novel full-scale Cross-dimension Self-attention U-Net with collaborative fusion of multi-scale feature for medical image segmentation

contributions.improvement: better discriminative and representational abilities among different scale features

contributions.improve_from: existing feature fusion methods like concatenation or addition

contributions.improvement: optimized semantic gap between encoders and decoders

contributions.improvement: efficient establishment of long-range dependencies in multiple dimensions
contributions.implementation_detail: The CS (Cross-dimension Self-attention) mechanism utilizes convolutions to capture local contextual weights and establishes long-range dependencies.

limitations: The performance of FCSU-Net can be further improved to meet higher requirements in medicine.
The process of compressing of CS mechanism in each dimension causes loss of spatial information.

title: Lightweight multi-scale dynamic selection network for medical image segmentation

contributions.improvement: simple architectures and low computational complexity while delivering relatively good performance

datasets.details: A public database of lung cancer CT image studies, collecting 1018 chest medical image files of 1010 different patients. The dataset has nearly 244,527 sliced images, with one CT image having 512x512 pixels. 1881 CT images of lung nodules were selected for segmentation experiments, with 70% used for training and 30% for testing. Images were pre-processed using Pylidc library, converted to '.png' format, and morphological processing techniques (K-mean clustering and morphological inflation) were applied to obtain lung regions.

experiment_setup.training_details: All neural networks use the same pipeline for training, including learning rate, optimizer, and random seed. The loss function chosen is the combined loss function of binary cross-entropy loss and dice coefficient loss. All input images are uniformly pre-processed. Networks are trained for 300 epochs using the AdamW optimizer with an initial learning rate of 5e-4 and a batch size of 4. Kaiming's initialization method is used. Experiments are implemented based on the PyTorch framework and run on a GeForce RTX 3090 GPU with 24G memory.

title: LMACV: A lightweight multiscale ACmix–VMamba framework for efficient multimodal medical image fusion

experiment_setup.training_details: The model was trained using cross-entropy loss for prediction-label discrepancies and contrastive loss to address cross-modal heterogeneity and enhance feature alignment. Both losses were backpropagated with weighted optimization. Advanced-stage glottic carcinoma cases (T3/T4) were included in the training cohort. Images were resized to 224x224 pixels, normalized to zero mean and unit variance (using ImageNet-derived parameters), and augmented with learnable positional encodings. Clinically relevant sentences were extracted from medical records using domain-specific prompts, and non-diagnostic content was filtered. The order of sentences within summaries was randomized during training.
